text: Navi Limited	Associate Product Manager I oa pattern ?

Problem Statement
You are given a 2D grid of size n \times m, representing a map of tasks. Each cell (i, j) contains an integer A[i][j]:
If A[i][j] > 0, it represents the time required to complete the work at that specific grid cell.
If A[i][j] = 0, the cell is empty (no work is required, but it can be traversed).
You start from a given starting position (or choose your starting position depending on the variant) and can move to any adjacent cell (up, down, left, right).
Each movement between two adjacent cells costs a fixed time of 2 units, regardless of whether the target cell has work or is empty (0).
To complete the work at a cell, you must spend the full work time specified by A[i][j] at that cell. Work at a cell is completed only once.
Your objective is to find the minimum total time required to visit and complete the work across the required cells

text:
At the close of another long week on the Meridian Stock Exchange, Mira has accumulated a backlog of n pending orders that she needs to send out to the market.

The i-th order has a notional size of p[i] lots.

The exchange's regulatory throttle limits each trader to at most c order submissions on any single day. Days are numbered 1, 2, 3, ..., starting from today.

The slippage cost grows a little each day, and a delayed order pays the price:

An order with notional size p[i] executed on day d incurs a slippage cost of d × p[i].

The total slippage cost is the sum of slippage costs across all orders Mira chooses to execute. Each order can be executed at most once.

Mira hasn't yet decided how many of her pending orders to push through this batch. She would like to know, for every possible workload, the minimum slippage cost achievable.

Task

For each k from 1 to n, determine the minimum total slippage cost Mira can incur if she chooses to execute exactly k orders, subject to the daily throttle limit of c orders per day.

Return all n answers in order:

answer for k = 1
answer for k = 2
...
answer for k = n
Function Description

Complete the function:

C++
vector<long> minSlippageCost(int c, vector<int> p)
Parameters

int c
 Maximum number of orders that can be executed in a single day.

int p[n]
 Array where p[i] is the notional size of the i-th order.

Returns
C++
vector<long>

An array of length n, where the k-th element (1-indexed) is the minimum total slippage cost achievable when executing exactly k orders.
